topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text:
I heard the news, and a chill took root in my bones. The oak, planted on the day I was but a lad, now lies in splinters. They say the lord needed more fields for the wheat, but what of the memories, the shade, the whispers of the saints that danced through its leaves on summer evenings? The ground where it stood, bare and []:
it speaks of futures overshadowed, of hands that hold the axe too eager to shape the world to their will. I look at the sky, at the cloudless expanse, and wonder where the rain will fall now that the old guardian is gone. May the saints watch over what's left of our peace.
